finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated into the query. An attacker can inject subqueries or boolean/time-based blind conditions (e.g. `sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)`) to extract data from any table in the SQLite DB. Stacked queries are not possible with PDO::query on sqlite, but blind extraction is.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: concatenated into SQL string and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, or quoting in list_users_sorted. Parameter binding cannot be used for identifiers and isn't used. The sibling list_users_safe (line 9-13) uses an allowlist and is safe. find_user (line 15-19) uses a prepared statement and is safe. No authentication or authorization checks exist in the file.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it unsanitized into the ORDER BY clause run by PDO::query, with no allowlist, cast or auth. The allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in the separate list_users_safe function. list_users_sorted is not called anywhere in the available code, so reachability depends on code outside this directory, but the function itself is exploitable by an anonymous caller.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause with no allowlist, cast or quoting, and nothing in the directory restricts the caller. The allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) is in a different function.
